newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Powerful quake rocks Venezuelan coast, 36 dead.
newsitem.headline: Powerful quake rocks Venezuelan coast, 36 dead.

text.p: Rescue teams pulled dead bodies and survivors from ruined buildings on Wednesday, after a quake measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale rocked the Caribbean coast killing at least 36 people, authorities said.
Office buildings and schools were flattened by the tremor -- Venezuela's worst for three decades -- and officials said the death toll could rise. Another 162 people were injured.

The majority of the deaths occurred in the small Caribbean town Cariaco about 295 miles (470 km) east of Caracas, where a high school collapsed, killing 22 people, mostly schoolchildren, Sucre state Governor Ramon Martinez told reporters.
Another six people died in the nearby town of Casanai, Martinez said.

In the historic state capital Cumana, at least eight dead bodies were retrieved from the rubble of a six-storey office building which "has crashed to the ground in a pile of cement and iron," according to a Reuters photographer who arrived at the scene late on Wednesday.
About two dozen rescue workers stood atop the 25 foot (8 metre) mound, picking their way slowly through the wreckage in search of survivors. Eight people had been pulled out alive late on Wednesday.
"We don't know exactly how many people have disappeared, but we know there are people alive beneath the rubble," Martinez said.
Another eight people trapped in the basement of what was left of the city-center building managed to contact the outside world by cellular telephone, Martinez said.
Up to 70 people were thought to have been in the building when the quake hit during office and school hours.

In the midst of a chaotic scene with hundreds of police, fire fighters and bystanders pushing in different directions, one young woman was carried out from the building on a stretcher, witnesses said.

Details from Cariaco were more sketchy due to a number of landslides blocking the road to the town. Preliminary reports said several buildings had collapsed including the school where 22 died. Martinez said seven children had been rescued from the school ruins alive and more could still be trapped inside.
"The information which we have received is sporadic and, I would say, is not very pleasant," said Civil Defense Director Francisco Daboin.

About 65 Red Cross and rescue workers left Caracas on an Air Force Hercules C130 late on Wednesday with more than 14 tonnes of supplies of medical supplies and heavy lifting equipment to assist in the rescue efforts.
The quake, the worst to hit Venezuela since 1967, struck at about 3:25 p.m. (1925 GMT) and measured 6.7 on the open-ended Richter scale, FUNVISIS seismological institute officials in Caracas said.
FUNVISIS officials earlier measured the quake at only about 5.5 on the Richter scale, although the U.S. Geological Survey in Golden, Colorado said it measured 6.9.
The epicenter was about 30 miles (49 km) off Venezuela's northeastern Caribbean coast and there were five aftershocks, the last at 5:40 p.m. (2140 GMT), they said.
FUNVISIS warned that further tremors and aftershocks could occur in coming days.

Despite the size of the quake, state-owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela said both production and export continued to flow smoothly. Venezuela is the largest exporter of gasoline to the United States.

Founded in 1521, Cumana is the oldest inhabited city in South America. However most of its colonial architecture was destroyed in a massive earthquake in 1797. Wednesday's earthquake was the second major tremor to strike the city of 250,000 people this century, the last in 1929.
The 1967 quake, the last to cause serious damage in Venezuela, killed 215 people in the capital and surrounding area, FUNVISIS officials said.
